subject.title: [Feature]: Pattern-based channel allowlist for Discord (glob/wildcard support)

question: Should Discord guild channel allowlists accept glob-style channel keys such as `ws-*`, and what exact precedence should they have relative to exact channel keys, thread-parent fallback, category inheritance, and literal `*`?
rationale: This is not a broken existing contract; it adds authorization-sensitive config syntax that could widen which Discord channels can trigger agents, so automation should not choose the product and security semantics.

options.title: Approve a narrow glob contract
options.body: Add documented Discord-owned glob support with exact/channel-parent matches before patterns, deterministic pattern ordering, literal `*` as the broad fallback, and focused security tests.

options.title: Defer to category and access redesign
options.body: Keep this issue open until the category-level and sender access-list decisions settle so dynamic channel admission is designed once.

options.title: Reject glob syntax
options.body: Keep exact channel keys plus literal `*` and direct users to category-level config if maintainers prefer less ambiguous authorization semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow glob contract
recommendation.body: Add documented Discord-owned glob support with exact/channel-parent matches before patterns, deterministic pattern ordering, literal `*` as the broad fallback, and focused security tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the shared matcher and Discord allow-list implementation that would carry the precedence decision.
